jobs.description: Wabash College, a liberal arts college for men located in Crawfordsville, Indiana, seeks applicants for a postdoctoral Scholar-in-Residenceto be housed in the Stephenson Institute for Classical Liberalism. Stephenson Institute postdoctoral Scholar-in-Residencies are residential fellowships that support full-time research and publication efforts. The duration of the appointment is one full academic year with the possibility of renewal for a second-year term. The disciplinary field, project design, and research approach are open. Successful applicants will have an interest in engaging with our students and participating in the intellectual life of the College and Institute during the fellowship, and will propose a project that contributes to one or more of the subject areas and research topics of particular interest to the Stephenson Institute’s mission:The institutional and cultural conditions of individual rights and legal equalityFree inquiry, free expression, free speech, and the market-place of ideasThe relationship(s) between market economies and government interventionThe role of personal responsibility in a free societyComparative and historical investigations of differing property rights regimesComparative political economy and comparative political philosophyApplicants are invited in their proposals to offer other ideas for how they might contribute to the Institute’s programming and areas of student engagement. While the primary focus of the position is research, the Scholar-in-Residence will also contribute to campus conversations via participation in Institute programming. There are no formal teaching expectations, but an undergraduate course offering may be arranged on an ad hoc basis and the discretion of the relevant academic department.Preferred start date is July 1, 2027. This position provides salary, benefits, private office space, relocation costs, and a fund to support research, travel, and related needs. Salary will be commensurate with relevant experience and academic field.About Wabash College and the Stephenson InstituteFounded in 1832, Wabash College is a private, independent, residential four-year liberal arts college with a mission to “educate men to think critically, act responsibly, lead effectively, and live humanely.” Its faculty is ranked No. 9 nationally for accessibility by the Princeton Review. The College invests significant resources to ensure students can participate in off-campus and international immersion learning experiences. Our 92-acre wooded campus is located in Crawfordsville, Indiana. Crawfordsville is a growing, vibrant community with easy access to outdoor recreation and facilities. Within 50 minutes of Indianapolis, Crawfordsville is close to an array of nationally recognized museums and sports facilities, including those housing the WNBA Fever, NBA Pacers, and NFL Colts.In the midst of a strategic transformation to advance the success of first-generation students and students from low-income families, Wabash College is committed to attracting and effectively supporting faculty and staff who are committed to student success. Approximately 25% of our students are federal Pell Grant recipients, one-third are first-generation college students, and about 20% identify as domestic students of color. Wabash offers a range of academic and cultural programs open to all members of the community. Wabash is a top-50 Liberal Arts College according toU.S. Newsand a member ofColleges That Change Lives. Many students, staff, and faculty find the close-knit community of the residential college one of the most rewarding aspects of joining the Wabash College community.Established in 2021, theStephenson Institute for Classical Liberalismis a non-partisan academic research center. It provides teaching, learning, and research opportunities for motivated students and faculty at Wabash College and beyond whom share an interest in the operations and implications of a free society.QualificationsApplicants should have a terminal degree in their academic field, and be no further than three years since completion of a Ph.D. To apply, go towww.wabash.edu/employmentand click the “Apply Now” button. D’Amico, director of the Stephenson Institute for Classical Liberalism at[email protected]. jobs.description: Case Western Reserve University (CWRU) is seeking a distinguished scholar to become the next Inamori Professor in Ethics and Director of the Inamori International Center for Ethics and Excellence (Inamori Center). We welcome exceptional candidates across all disciplines, with particular interest in research focused on the ethics of artificial intelligence, technology, and neuroscience, that engages the humanities, engineering and/or medicine. The Director role provides a meaningful platform to build and strengthen interdisciplinary engagement across the University, bringing people and ideas together, developing new initiatives and partnerships, and advancing scholarship, teaching, and dialogue around consequential ethical questions, while maintaining scholarly engagement.CWRU’s strengths in engineering and medicine are complemented by growing investment at the intersection of the humanities and emerging technologies. A$125 million giftfrom the Mandel Foundation in 2026 includes support for a new humanities building and funding for integrating humanities with STEM approaches, while the University’s new $300 millionInterdisciplinary Science and Engineering Buildingbrings together researchers across Arts and Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine. This environment creates fertile ground for the Director to forge connections across artificial intelligence, technology, engineering, medicine, neuroscience, the humanities, and other fields, engaging scholars, students, and external partners around some of the most consequential ethical questions facing society.The Director will also provide leadership for the Inamori Ethics Prize, the Center’s prestigious international award recognizing individuals whose ethical leadership has significantly improved the condition of humankind. The Center works across academic disciplines and with local and global partners to promote ethical leadership and address complex ethical questions through scholarship, education, student experiences, and public dialogue.In addition to the Inamori Ethics Prize, the Center supports faculty scholarship, curricular and co-curricular initiatives, student mentorship, service-learning opportunities, and public programming.Learn more about theInamori Centerand view the complete list ofInamori Ethics Prize recipients.KEY RESPONSIBILITIESThe Inamori Professor and Director will provide intellectual, strategic, and administrative leadership for the Inamori International Center for Ethics and Excellence. articulate a compelling vision for the Center’s next chapter and translate that vision into programs, partnerships, and initiatives with meaningful impact.Advance the Center as an interdisciplinary hub for ethical inquiry, connecting scholars and practitioners across fields and schools, and providing ethics support for complex research projects that include a significant ethical dimension.Develop programming that engages consequential ethical questions emerging from areas such as artificial intelligence, technology, engineering, medicine, neuroscience, the humanities, and other disciplines.Provide leadership for the Inamori Ethics Prize and identify opportunities to increase its visibility, reach, and impact.Provide effective administrative and operational leadership for the Center, including stewardship of its approximately $400,000 annual budget.Serve as a visible ambassador for the Center and strengthen its national and international profile.MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONSThe successful candidate will bring:A record of scholarship and academic achievement appropriate for appointment at the rank of full professor with tenure at Case Western Reserve University.International recognition as a scholar and thought leader in their field.An outstanding record of excellence in research, teaching, and mentorship.A scholarly focus in ethics or demonstrated integration of ethical inquiry into their scholarship and teaching.A strong record of interdisciplinary engagement and collaboration.Demonstrated leadership experience within an academic or research environment.The ability to develop and advance a compelling strategic vision for the Inamori Center.About Case Western Reserve UniversityAs the fastest-growing research university in the United States, Case Western Reserve University is a force in career-defining education and life-changing research. Across our campus, more than 12,000 students from around the world converge to seek knowledge, find solutions and accelerate their impact. CWRU's programs span a wide range of fields, but the spaces of their convergence is where we thrive: where law meets management, engineering meets entrepreneurship, arts meets science, and medicine, nursing, dentistry and social work unite to improve human health. And with our location in Cleveland, Ohio—a hub of cultural, business and healthcare activity—our students gain unparalleled access to academic, research, clinical and entrepreneurial opportunities that prepare them to join our network of more than 128,000 alumni worldwide.Research is central to the University’s academic enterprise, with more than $600 million in research conducted annually. jobs.description: Purdue University invites applications for a  3 year (12 month FY contract) Postdoctoral Research Associate position. Our team will systematically examine how these neglected safeguards protect both civic and economic freedoms and expand awareness of their role in doing so for both scholarly and civic audiences.We are looking for a postdoctoral research associate to conduct research on one or more of the neglected safeguards of liberalism. jobs.description:
About the projectThe University of Notre Dame Australia is proud to host the Arabic and Hebrew teams of the European Research Council (ERC) Synergy project, “Logic in Reverse Redux: Illegitimate Argumentative Moves in the Arabic, Byzantine, Hebrew and Latin Medieval Traditions,” (RevLogRedux), which is to run until 30 April 2031. The coordinating team of the Synergy Grant is led by Leone Gazziero at the CNRS, France; the Arabic team leader at UNDA is Tony Street and the Hebrew team leader is Charles Manekin. We seek to appoint up to twohighly research-active scholars working in medieval Hebrew philosophy with a track-record, or an interest in developing expertise, in researching medieval logical texts and fallacy-theory. In accordance with ERC conditions, all outcomes are to be published Open Access.About the roleThe Hebrew Traditionteam of the ERC project, “Logic in Reverse Redux: Illegitimate Argumentative Moves in the Arabic, Byzantine, Hebrew and Latin Medieval Traditions,” seeks to appoint up to two postdoctoral researchers. Participation in the project will be an opportunity to acquire new textual and philosophical skills, produce a significant research portfolio, develop ties with leading researchers in medieval philosophy, and be part of a major initiative in digital humanities. The team will engage actively with the other teams working on the Latin, Byzantine, Arabic rational and Arabic traditional sciences.As a guide, appointees will be expected to devote their time as follows: 20% transcribing, editing and translating a number of texts; 20% responding to the initiatives of the Geneva team as they develop AskSten; 60% conducting independent research on the historical and cultural context of the texts studied, and analysis of the fallacy-theories developed by Hebrew authors, especially as they relate to Aristotle’s Sophistical Refutations.These research-focused positions will contribute to the University's strategic research goals through the production of high-impact publications, including ERC-related outputs targeting leading Q1 journals or scholarly monographs. The role will strengthen the research profile of the Centre for the History of Philosophy, particularly in the growing field of Hebrew Philosophy, while supporting grant applications, research supervision and mentoring, and engaging in academic, professional, and research administration activities.
Key ResponsibilitiesContribute to the production of critical editions and translations of a corpus of medieval Hebrew texts on fallacies (seeherefor passages to be edited), preferably as the sole editor and translator for assigned passages, or, where necessary, as a team member working under the supervision of Professor Manekin.Undertake the transcription of texts not yet available in electronic format for inclusion in the project's web-based database.Conduct primary research on the historical and cultural context of the texts studied, and analysis of the fallacy-theories developed by Hebrew authors, especially as they relate to Aristotle’s Sophistical Refutations.Collaborate with the University of Geneva team in integrating materials from four philosophical traditions into AskSten, a multi-layered virtual research environment whose digital archive, knowledge base, Semantic Web architecture, and online deployment will enhance the formal expressiveness and coherence of the project's findings; seehttps://www.unige.ch/RevLog/about-1.Contribute to all activities associated with the ERC Synergy Grant, includingparticipating in conferences and workshops in the UK and Europe, help in organisingconferences and workshops, translation, independent research on topics related to the texts to be edited, and liaison with teams at CNRS, the University of Lille, and the University of Geneva to advance the project's objectives of collaboration and synergy.Post-docs are expected to participate in person in a fortnightly team seminar through the semester at the Broadway Campus.Qualifications, skills & experience
Essential:Research-level proficiency in the philosophical language of medieval Hebrew.Doctoral level training in Hebrew philosophy or medieval Jewish intellectual history, with evidence of potential for high-quality research; a strong publication record is highly desirable.Proficiency in Hebrew text entry, with the ability to read and interpret medieval manuscripts.Desirable:Background in digital humanities.Facility in another language in RevLog’s coverage (Latin, classical Greek, Arabic) or relevant to the study of the broader translation movement (Syriac).
